title: Inverse image preserves scalar matrices and their cokernels
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $R=\Lambda(*)$, and let $h:V\to U$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use their small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], coefficient rings $\Lambda_U,\Lambda_V$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], canonical ring isomorphism $\alpha_h:h^{-1}\Lambda_U\cong\Lambda_V$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], and module pullback $h^*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. For $m,n\geq0$ and a matrix $A=(a_{ij})\in\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(R)$, let $A_U:\Lambda_U^m\to\Lambda_U^n$ and $A_V:\Lambda_V^m\to\Lambda_V^n$ act by the images of the same entries under the canonical scalar maps [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Here finite free modules and cokernels use [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. The regular-module comparison induced by $\alpha_h$, and its finite-coproduct extensions $e_r:h^*(\Lambda_U^r)\cong\Lambda_V^r$, satisfy $e_n\circ h^*(A_U)=A_V\circ e_m$. They induce an isomorphism $h^*\operatorname{coker}(A_U)\cong\operatorname{coker}(A_V)$ compatible with the cokernel projections.

proof.text: Let d:1→Λ be the condensed section obtained from the scalar a:ℤ→Λ(*) by the constant-sheaf adjunction counit. Expanding scalarSection shows scalarSection_W(a)=ε(p_W*) p_W*(d). For P=p_W*, the identity on PΛ identifies the transported regular module with regular(PΛ). Regular_hom_ext and one_comp_regularLift then identify P applied to multiplication by d with the regular endomorphism defined by scalarSection_W(a). Naturality of upperStarFromPointComp h at this condensed regular endomorphism gives F(t_a,U) α=α t_a,V. This uses the same canonical scalar a on both schemes. Explicit source and target object arguments in the naturality application keep Lean from unfolding the composite geometric pullback functors.

proof.text: The identity on FΛ_U identifies the transported regular module with regular(FΛ_U). Identify this identity morphism with mapModUnitIso.inv by composing with mapModUnitIso.hom and canceling that isomorphism; no unfolding of a chosen inverse is required. The existing regularExtensionIso along α identifies its extension of scalars with regular Λ_V. Their composite is exactly the unchanged scalarMatrixRegularPullbackIso. The extension comparison is already constructed and proved by the extension–restriction adjunction and the universal property of the regular module; no separate mixed-bimodule right-unitor argument is needed here. The sheaf tensor structure supplies the ambient hypotheses.

proof.text: Use the existing preservesFiniteColimits_upperStar and upperStar_additive instances of the module pullback. The functor mapBiproduct followed by biproduct.mapIso of the regular comparison is exactly the unchanged scalarMatrixFreePullbackIso. The canonical mapBiproduct injection/projection identities and the biproduct.map identities describe this comparison for every finite rank, including zero.

proof.text: Let e identify the transported regular module with the regular module over FΛ_U, using the identity underlying morphism. Conjugate mapMod(F)(t_a,U) by e to get a regular endomorphism p. Because both e and its inverse have identity underlying maps, the equation p.hom α=α t_a,V.hom is precisely the naturality square of step 1. Apply regularExtensionIso_naturality to p and t_a,V, precompose by the extended e.hom, and cancel the adjacent extended e.hom and e.inv. The result is scalarRegular_pullback for the unchanged canonical regular comparison.

proof.text: Conjugate the pulled-back scalarMatrix by the finite-free comparisons. Apply biproduct.hom_ext' to the input injections and biproduct.hom_ext to the output projections. The mapBiproduct and biproduct.map identities reduce each entry to the scalarRegular_pullback identity of step 4. Cancel the inverse regular comparison to identify the entries. Cancel the inverse finite-free comparison to obtain the required square. The same universal properties cover empty source or target ranks.

proof.text: Use PreservesCokernel.iso for module pullback, which preserves finite colimits and zero morphisms, to identify the pullback of the source cokernel with the cokernel of the pulled-back matrix. Compose with cokernel.mapIso induced by the matrix square and the two finite-free comparisons. The two canonical cokernel projection identities, PreservesCokernel.π_iso_hom and cokernel.π_map, give precisely the required compatibility.

lean.statement: theorem scalarMatrix_inverseImage {m n : ℕ} (A : Fin m → Fin n → (𝟙_ Ab.{u + 1} ⟶ scalarRingObj Λ)) : (CondensedRing.upperStar Λ h).map (scalarMatrix Λ U A) ≫ (scalarMatrixFreePullbackIso Λ h n).hom = (scalarMatrixFreePullbackIso Λ h m).hom ≫ scalarMatrix Λ V A ∧ ∃ e : (CondensedRing.upperStar Λ h).obj (cokernel (scalarMatrix Λ U A)) ≅ cokernel (scalarMatrix Λ V A), (CondensedRing.upperStar Λ h).map (cokernel.π (scalarMatrix Λ U A)) ≫ e.hom = (scalarMatrixFreePullbackIso Λ h n).hom ≫ cokernel.π (scalarMatrix Λ V A)
